function.uniprot_function: Segment polarity protein dishevelled homolog DVL-1 is a cytoplasmic scaffold protein that transduces Wnt signaling from Frizzled receptors to downstream effectors. DVL1 participates in both canonical Wnt/beta-catenin signaling and non-canonical Wnt pathways including planar cell polarity and Wnt/Ca2+ pathways. Upon Wnt pathway activation, phosphorylated DVL translocates to the plasma membrane through interaction between the DVL PDZ domain and the FZD KTxxxW motif. DVL1 mediates signal transduction for multiple Wnt ligands, enabling LEF1 activation during WNT1 and WNT3A signaling. DVL1 binds to the cytoplasmic C-terminus of Frizzled family members and is required for Wnt-induced LRP6 phosphorylation and signalosome assembly. DVL1 forms polymers that recruit AXIN1/GSK3B complexes to the membrane, promoting formation of signalosomes that inhibit the beta-catenin destruction complex.
function.catalytic_activity: Not an enzyme; functions as scaffold protein
function.tissue_specificity: Expressed in adult brain, placenta, lung, liver, and kidney with same patterns in fetal tissues. In embryonic development, expressed in neural tube (particularly dorsal portions), optic stalk, ventral forebrain, midbrain, eye, spinal cord, and notochord. In neurons, localizes to dendrites and axons associated with microtubules and actin-rich regions. Low brain regional specificity in adults.

pathways.pathway_role_summary: DVL1 is a central scaffold protein in Wnt signaling pathways. In canonical Wnt/beta-catenin signaling, DVL1 is recruited to the plasma membrane via PDZ domain binding to FZD receptors. Upon Wnt stimulation, DVL1 undergoes CK1-mediated phosphorylation and K63-linked ubiquitination, forming polymers that recruit AXIN1/GSK3B complexes to the membrane. This signalosome assembly promotes LRP6 phosphorylation by CK1γ and inhibits the beta-catenin destruction complex, leading to beta-catenin stabilization and TCF/LEF-mediated transcription. DVL1 stability is regulated by KLHL12-mediated ubiquitination (binding PGXPP degron with Kd ~22 μM) and deubiquitination by USP14 and CYLD. DVL1 also participates in non-canonical Wnt pathways including planar cell polarity and Wnt/Ca2+ signaling.

disease_associations.description: Frameshift mutations in penultimate exon (exon 14) cause autosomal dominant Robinow syndrome. 15 pathogenic DVL1 variants identified (ClinVar). Mutations produce -1 frameshift replacing C-terminus with novel highly basic, proline-rich sequence (gain-of-function). Examples: c.1644del (p.F549Sfs*125), c.1575_1582dup (p.Pro528ArgfsTer149). Mutant DVL1 fails to change localization in response to Wnt ligands and cannot activate canonical Wnt signaling in TOPFlash assays. Clinical features include mesomelic limb shortening, genital hypoplasia, and orofacial abnormalities.

DVL1 aberrations implicated in colorectal cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma, and basal cell carcinoma through aberrant Wnt pathway activation. DVL1 overexpression correlates with tumor progression and metastasis in some cancers.
DVL1 expression alterations observed in intracranial meningioma; role in tumor development under investigation

metadata.data_quality_notes: High-quality data with extensive experimental validation. Sequence obtained from UniProt O14640. Domain coordinates from multiple sources show minor variation (InterPro: DIX 1-82, PDZ 249-342, DEP 404-502; Pfam: DIX 3-81, PDZ 244-343, DEP 428-497). Used InterPro coordinates as primary reference. PGXPP degron motif well-characterized with crystal structure (PDB 6TTK). Binding affinity to KLHL12 measured at Kd ~22 μM. Phosphorylation sites S143 and T224 experimentally validated for CK1ε/δ. K63-linked ubiquitination at K50 and K48-linked at K285 experimentally confirmed. Most kinetic data from DVL2/DVL3 studies; DVL family members show high conservation and functional overlap. Specific Km, kcat values for deubiquitinases not available in literature. CYLD phosphorylation regulation (S418, S568) well-characterized with temporal kinetics (5 min post-stimulation). AlphaFold model shows high confidence for structured domains, low confidence for IDRs as expected. 131 total interactors in BioGRID; top 20 high-confidence interactors identified from STRING. All interactions include unique IDs and site-specific binding information where available.
metadata.modeling_relevance_summary: DVL1 is critical for Kappa-based Wnt signaling pathway modeling. Key features: (1) DIX domain mediates head-to-tail polymerization with AXIN1 DAX domain - essential for signalosome assembly with well-defined binding interfaces; (2) PDZ domain binds FZD KTxxxW motif for membrane recruitment; (3) PGXPP degron (658-663) binds KLHL12 with Kd ~22 μM enabling quantitative modeling of constitutive ubiquitination; (4) S143/T224 phosphorylation by CK1ε creates switch-like behavior; (5) K63-ubiquitination at K50 vs K48-ubiquitination at K285 enables modeling of signaling vs degradation outcomes; (6) Dynamic regulation by USP14 and CYLD deubiquitinases (CYLD inhibited by phosphorylation within 5 min of TNF-α); (7) Multiple binding partners with distinct interfaces (AXIN1 DIX-DAX, FZD PDZ-KTxxxW, LRP6 for signalosome) suitable for multi-component complex modeling. Intrinsically disordered regions between domains may provide flexibility for scaffold assembly. Disease mutations (Robinow syndrome) demonstrate functional importance of C-terminal region. Unique interaction IDs distinguish different interaction types; deduplicated interactions prevent counting same partner multiple times.
